items.title: Trump faces backlash after saying he 'convinced' Nvidia to reinstate CEO Jensen Huang
items.line: Nvidia had come under pressure from President Trump to reappoint Huang, whose comeback helped add $1tn to the company's stock value.
items.body: Nvidia has reinstated CEO Jensen Huang just days after rejecting his offer to return to the AI chipmaker - and less than two weeks after he was forced to resign over a reported affair with a suspected Chinese spy. The company came under pressure by Donald Trump to reappoint Huang - and on Monday, the US president said he "made the deal" to "convince" the tech giant's board to bring him back.

items.title: RMA expert questions Fonterra's application to dump 22m litres of milk
items.line: A resource management practitioner said there were already provisions in the RMA that allowed for emergency milk dumping.
items.body: A resource management expert is questioning Fonterra's rationale in applying for consent to dump up to 22 million litres of raw milk in Canterbury. The dairy giant has applied to the regional council to vary the conditions of seven consents, arguing approval is needed because of a forecast milk surplus due to processing constraints in the South Island.

items.title: Beef mince sold at Auckland supermarket recalled over possible metal pieces
items.line: Food Safety deputy director-general Vincent Arbuckle says the small metal pieces could cause injury if consumed.
items.body: Beef mince that was sold at an Auckland supermarket is being recalled over concerns it may contain small pieces of metal. New Zealand Food Safety says Pak'nSave Highland Park is recalling made-in-store beef mince and prime beef mince as the products may contain foreign matter. "The concern with these products is that they may contain small metal pieces, which could cause injury if consumed," said New Zealand Food Safety deputy director-general Vincent Arbuckle.

items.title: What strike on Russian ship in Libya says about spread of Ukraine war
items.line: Ukraine's sinking of a Russian battleship at a port in Libya raises the stakes of the war a notch, writes Frank Gardner.
items.body: Anchored in a Mediterranean harbour nearly 2,000 miles from Moscow, the Captain of Russia's corvette Merkury might well have thought his ship was safe from attack. It wasn't. The audacious and successful night-time attack in Benghazi , co-ordinated by Ukraine's SBU intelligence agency and its armed forces, has raised the obvious question: is the Ukraine war spreading well beyond its borders?

items.title: RNZ Chief People Officer Sarah Neilson leaves amid financial crisis
items.line: The news of Sarah Neilson’s departure was made in a message to staff on Tuesday afternoon.
items.body: RNZ's human resources boss Sarah Neilson is leaving the public broadcaster, the third senior executive to depart amid its financial crisis. The Crown entity confirmed on Tuesday that Neilson, its chief people officer, would finish on Friday. Her departure follows those of chief executive Paul Thompson and chief financial officer Hilary Parker, as an independent inquiry looms into RNZ's shock $11.8 million loss this last financial year.

items.title: Christchurch’s $17.6m Brougham Street bridge opens to the public
items.line: Pedestrians, cyclists and scooters can now cross Brougham Street without stopping traffic.
items.body: Radiating like a 37m-long David Bain jersey, Christchurch’s Brougham St bridge is finally open to pedestrians, cyclists and scooters. The $17.6 million structure is unmissable to traffic travelling east and west on Brougham St, and potentially to those orbiting Earth aboard the space station; such is the striking red and yellow colour scheme. Previously, vehicles approaching or leaving SH76 were brought to a halt to allow a steady stream of pedestrians and cyclists to get across one of the busiest roads in Christchurch.

items.title: TVNZ staff call off 24-hour strike
items.line: Union members were due to walk off the job for 24 hours from 12.01am Wednesday, but this has now been averted.
items.body: A spokesperson for the union says progress was made during mediation this afternoon and an improved offer has will be taken back to members. TVNZ staff had earlier issued a strike notice for 24 hours tomorrow over a pay rise dispute. Staff were seeking a 5 percent pay rise, rather than the 2.5 percent TVNZ had offered. TVNZ said it had been in constructive bargaining discussions since July, but had not reached an agreement.

items.title: Cricket: Black Caps face 'a war of attrition' to save India test
items.line: The best of the batting conditions are over as the Black Caps attempt to save the first test against India.
items.body: The best of the batting conditions are likely to be over as the Black Caps attempt to save the first test against India. New Zealand will resume their second innings on 119 for two, still trailing India by 233 runs and facing 90 overs on what could be a variable wicket on the final day at the Basin Reserve. "We're pretty behind the game, obviously," Rachin Ravindra said at the end of the day. "It was a good period to get through two down."

items.title: Former Silver Ferns captain Julie Carter remembered as competitive, clever and committed
items.line: Former Silver Ferns captain Julie Carter remembered as competitive, clever and committed.
items.body: "Competitive" and "committed" are some of the words teammates of former Silver Ferns captain Julie Carter are using to describe her, as news of her death reaches the far corners of the netball community. Netball New Zealand on Monday said it was deeply saddened to share the news that Carter had died, aged 60. "Jules", or "JC" as she was often referred by her teammates, played 50 Tests for New Zealand between 1986 and 1993.

items.title: Nicalis removes AI-generated music from The Binding of Isaac: Repentance+ after player backlash
items.line: Nicalis has pulled AI-generated music from The Binding of Isaac: Repentance+ after players discovered it in the game's latest update, prompting a wave of negative Steam reviews.
items.body: Nicalis has pulled AI-generated music from The Binding of Isaac: Repentance+ after players discovered it in the game's latest update, prompting a wave of negative Steam reviews. The music - tied to a run themed around Grand Theft Auto 6 - released on November 19, the same day GTA 6 launched. The following day, a player claimed the music was "100% generated by Suno (AI) (with proof)," highlighting tracks whose metadata referenced the AI music tool Suno.

COP31 ends in failure as countries split over fossil fuels, climate finance
items.line: COP31 ended without a consensus deal for the first time since 2009.
items.body: ANTALYA, Turkey—By the time the United Nations COP31 climate talks ended Sunday afternoon, the conference center resembled a going-out-of-business sale at a pawnshop for broken dreams. As cleaning crews cleared away the debris left by more than 100,000 participants, Murat Kurum, president of the Conference of the Parties and Turkey’s minister of environment, urbanization, and climate change, tried to tie together disparate parts of a draft climate deal with a shiny ribbon of multilateralism.

items.title: Eruption Extends Iwo Jima’s Beach
items.line: A volcanic eruption just off the southeast shore of the Pacific island has reshaped the coast, but it’s unclear how long the new land will survive.
items.body: A volcanic eruption just off the southeast shore of the Pacific island has reshaped the coast, but it’s unclear how long the new land will survive. A volcanic eruption in the shallows near Iwo Jima has extended the Japanese island’s famed black sand beaches, at least temporarily. Signs of unrest began in late October 2026. On October 27, seismic sensors recorded a sharp uptick in activity, and Japan’s Meteorological Agency reported that the first photographs of the eruption were captured.

Sky New Zealand Sets ‘I Will Find You: The Search For Alysha Hanin’ True Crime Series From Woodcut International & Our Story
items.line: EXCLUSIVE: An upcoming three-part true crime series out of the UK and New Zealand will investigate the 2002 disappearance of mother and model Alysha Hanin.
items.body: EXCLUSIVE: An upcoming three-part true crime series out of the UK and New Zealand will investigate the 2002 disappearance of mother and model Alysha Hanin. Sky New Zealand has greenlit I Will Find You: The Search For Alysha Hanin from local producer Our Story and the UK-based Woodcut International, which has picked up international distribution rights. Production is currently ongoing ahead of a scheduled Q2 2027 launch, with New Zealand On Air supporting.

items.title: NASA Awards Contract for NOAA’s Near Earth Orbit Network Program
items.line: NASA, on behalf of the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA), has awarded a contract to Northrop Grumman Systems Corporation for the Sounder for Microwave-Based Applications (SMBA)…
items.body: NASA, on behalf of the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA), has awarded a contract to Northrop Grumman Systems Corporation for the Sounder for Microwave-Based Applications (SMBA) instruments on NOAA’s Near Earth Orbit Network (NEON) satellites. The cost-plus-fixed-fee, firm-fixed-price, and time-and-materials hybrid contract has a value of $290.6 million. The period of performance runs from Nov. 23 through April 1, 2042. The work will take place at the awardee’s facility.

items.line: Kagi, which already offers a paid alternative to Google Search and its own Orion browser as a rival to Chrome, is taking on another Google service: Gmail.
items.body: Posts from this topic will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed. Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed. Today, Kagi announced a public beta of Kagi Mail, a new email service that has “no surveillance, no ads, open standards, and no lock-in.”

AJ Brimson confirms future, Titans departure locked in
items.line: The star fullback has a new club.
items.body: The PNG Chiefs have confirmed AJ Brimson will join as the tenth player for 2028, with his Gold Coast Titans departure locked in. Brimson has been looking for a way out of the Titans for some time, with the club unable to secure him as the number one jumper. With Keano Kini taking over there, and Jayden Campbell preferred as the first-choice five-eighth, Brimson has been shuffled out to the centres on a majority of occasions.

items.title: Ben Hunt’s likely 2027 role revealed as Broncos grapple big spine questions
items.line: The club is looking to find their Adam Reynolds replacement.
items.body: Brisbane Broncos have a favourite for an Adam Reynolds replacement for the 2027 season. The Broncos are looking to return to the finals after finishing 14th this past season, with 2025 being their premiership-winning season. In 2027, the club will not have Payne Haas and Adam Reynolds , who have left. Payne Haas went to the South Sydney Rabbitohs , while Reynolds confirmed his retirement.

Jamal Fogarty makes call about his future with Manly
items.line: The Sea Eagles are reportedly interested in releasing their halfback.
items.body: Manly Sea Eagles halfback Jamal Fogarty has decided where his future lies after reports surfaced that the club wanted to release the veteran playmaker. Reports have recently surfaced that the club wants to release players on massive contracts to create salary cap flexibility. Fogarty, along with Luke Brooks and Ethan Bullemor , have been Manly's candidates to find new clubs. According to Fox Sports , Fogarty wants to play out his contract at the Northern Beaches after reports surfaced of a swap with the Tigers for Latu Fainu .
